solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: 'Former PM missing Queen' shock

indicators.note: missing says the Queen's letters are absent from the former Prime Minister's name

parts.note: Margaret Thatcher was UK Prime Minister 1979-1990
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual crossword Queen

explanation.surface: A newspaper headline reports the startling news that an ex-premier has lost the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make the first four words look like a headline, but they are the wordplay; 'shock' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A shock of hair is a thick mass of it, as is a thatch of hair.

clue.text: Kilted sailor half-heartedly beaten

indicators.note: half-heartedly means losing half of the heart, one of the two middle letters

parts.note: tanned means beaten, as in tanning someone's hide

explanation.surface: A seaman in a kilt is thrashed with little enthusiasm.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone wearing a kilt is clad in plaid cloth, the Scottish check fabric.

clue.text: Examiner of car on hill

parts.note: Audi is a German make of car
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A vehicle inspector looks at a car parked on a slope.
explanation.definitionFit: An auditor examines a company's accounts, so is an inspector of finances.

clue.text: It's useful when altering speed in mail armour?

definitions.meaning: a gear system using a chain, as on a bicycle, for changing speed
chain mail is armour, so ... is whimsically armour worn as gear

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is whimsical: chain mail could be called chain gear, kit made of chain.
explanation.definitionFit: A bicycle's derailleur moves the chain between cogs to alter speed.

clue.text: One broadcasts in Sweden and Portugal with university don

parts.note: S is the international vehicle code for Sweden
P is the international vehicle code for Portugal
a reader is a senior university lecturer in Britain

explanation.surface: Someone who scatters news is found in Iberia and Scandinavia alongside an academic.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that scatters seed or grit spreads it about, so it broadcasts in the farming sense.

clue.text: Nancy's lower middle-class with terrible repetitious gob

definitions.note: Nancy is a French city, so the French term is wanted

indicators.note: terrible means awful, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A snobbish remark about a suburban woman with a mouth that keeps saying the same things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nancy' looks like a woman's name but is the city in France, signalling a French phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase for the small-business or shopkeeping class is literally small citizen.

clue.text: Call out as convenient during previous day

indicators.note: during means inside the period, so the word sits within the day

explanation.surface: Someone shouts that yesterday would suit.
explanation.definitionFit: To call up or summon a memory or feeling is to bring it out.

clue.text: Reforming could make Bluebeard be this strong

indicators.note: reforming means reshaping, so the letters of the pirate's name are rearranged

explanation.surface: Reforming the murderous Bluebeard would make him tough.
explanation.walkthrough: Composite anagram: BLUEBEARD's letters are the answer plus BE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lasting and hard-wearing is sturdy, so strong in the sense of long-lived.

clue.text: Slice is more risky

definitions.meaning: comparative of rash, meaning more reckless

explanation.definitionFit: A bacon strip is a slice, and someone more reckless is more risky.

clue.text: 5's hope to be this unexpectedly may and will be proud

indicators.note: unexpectedly means surprisingly, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Social climbers may hope to rise and will be proud if they do.
explanation.walkthrough: 5 is PETIT BOURGEOIS, the lower middle class, which hopes to rise socially.
explanation.definitionFit: Climbing the social ladder is what the aspiring lower middle class is said to hope for.

clue.text: Yorkshire resort's favourite celebrity treatment

parts.note: Redcar is a seaside town in North Yorkshire
a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet

explanation.surface: A famous visitor gets VIP treatment when visiting a northern seaside town.
explanation.definitionFit: Rolling out a crimson carpet for arrivals is the standard way of greeting famous guests, hence the idiom.

clue.text: Monstrous female cut short her menfolk?

definitions.note: plural: the male monsters of an ogress's kind

indicators.note: cut short says the last letter is dropped from the monster's name

parts.note: an ogress is a female ogre

explanation.surface: A shrewish woman is snubbed, leaving one to wonder about the men in her life.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition depends on the wordplay: 'her' is the monstrous female, so her menfolk are male monsters of the same type; hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The male counterparts of a female giant are the brutish giants of the same folk-tale race.

clue.text: Feeler to introduce 'Fingers' for example to Anna

indicators.note: to introduce means to put something into the name that follows

parts.note: you have ten fingers, so fingers exemplify the number ten

explanation.surface: Someone tries to sound out a woman by presenting a pickpocket nicknamed Fingers.
explanation.definitionFit: An insect's antenna is its feeler, used to sense its surroundings by touch.

clue.text: Quiver of young soprano enthralling Frenchman

indicators.note: enthralling means holding captive, so the singer holds the Frenchman inside

parts.note: a treble is a boy soprano
M is the abbreviation for Monsieur

explanation.surface: A boy chorister's voice shakes with excitement over a dashing Frenchman.
explanation.definitionFit: To quiver is to shake slightly, the same as to shake with fear or cold.

clue.text: Essentially more affected by beer? That's frightening

indicators.note: essentially means at its core, so only the inner letters are kept

parts.note: beerier means more under the influence of beer

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether being drunker on ale makes things scarier.
explanation.definitionFit: Something weird and spooky is unsettling, so the word means frightening in a ghostly way.

clue.text: This may be cut or stored in purpose-built depots

indicators.note: stored in says the little word is kept inside the reshaped depots
purpose-built means constructed anew, so the letters of depots are rebuilt

explanation.surface: Something gets cut or kept in specially built warehouses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' suggests a key or a step, but in Britain a doorstep is a very thick slice of bread. 'purpose-built' gives DOSTEP, which 'stored in' opens to hold the little word.
explanation.definitionFit: A doorstep sandwich uses a very thick slice cut from the loaf, so it is something cut.

clue.text: Sailor in insignificant illumination

indicators.note: in places the sailor inside the word for insignificant

explanation.surface: A seaman sits in dim light.
explanation.definitionFit: Light coming from stars is a faint natural illumination of the night sky.

clue.text: To embrace poetry socialist went back

indicators.note: to embrace means to hold inside, so the socialist wraps around the poetry

explanation.surface: A left-winger retreated rather than accept poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: To go in the opposite direction is to back up or retreat, so went back.

clue.text: Perhaps one that's deserted salver carrying drink? Just the reverse

indicators.note: carrying says one piece holds another inside
just the reverse swaps the roles, so the drink holds the salver

explanation.surface: A waiter with a tray of drinks may have abandoned their post.
explanation.walkthrough: Read plainly, 'carrying' has the salver holding the drink; 'Just the reverse' flips the roles so the drink holds the salver.
explanation.definitionFit: A deserter is one example of someone disloyal, hence the 'Perhaps'.

clue.text: Apply space energy

parts.note: an en is a printer's unit of space

explanation.surface: Bring energy to bear on outer space.
explanation.definitionFit: To put a law into effect is to apply it, making people comply.

clue.text: Saw commercial article, as an example, being sent back

indicators.note: being sent back means the pieces are read backwards

explanation.surface: An advert, with an item cited as an example, is returned.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old saying or proverb, an older sense of the word.

clue.text: Dead quiet after a time

indicators.note: after places the word for quiet behind the other pieces

explanation.surface: Total silence follows for a while.
explanation.definitionFit: A euphemism used of the departed, who are said to rest at peace.

clue.text: Bat somehow saved from disastrous swallow dive

indicators.note: somehow means in some unexplained way, so the letters are rearranged
disastrous means a mess, signalling the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A cricket bat is somehow rescued from a botched dive.
explanation.walkthrough: Composite anagram: SWALLOW DIVE rearranged is the answer plus SAVED. Cricket bats are traditionally made of willow wood.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket bats are made from willow wood, so the word stands for the bat.

clue.text: Conclude drama in hell

explanation.surface: A play ends in hellish chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: Dante's name for the underworld became the general word for a place of fiery torment.

clue.text: No time for Privy Councillor to go on European river

indicators.note: no means without, so the time letter is removed

parts.note: Privy Councillors are styled Rt Hon, Right Honourable

explanation.surface: A senior politician has no time to go to a continental river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rhône is a major river of Switzerland and France, flowing to the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Cut out City's ridiculous spiel

parts.note: EC is the postcode area of the City of London

indicators.note: ridiculous means absurd, so the letters of spiel are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone tells a financial institution to stop its absurd sales pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: To outshine or overshadow something is to cut it out of the light, as the moon does the sun.

clue.text: Broad and slow old boat used by learner

parts.note: L is a learner, from L-plates
the Argo was Jason's ship in Greek myth

explanation.surface: An ancient vessel, wide and sluggish, is handed over to a novice.
explanation.definitionFit: The musical direction means broad, at a slow and stately tempo.

clue.text: I inform girl this substance can promote cleavage

parts.note: to sing is slang for informing to the police

explanation.surface: Someone tips a young woman off about a product that enhances her bosom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cleavage' is not the neckline: isinglass is also a name for mica, a mineral that splits easily into thin sheets.
explanation.definitionFit: Mica, called isinglass, has perfect cleavage, splitting cleanly into thin layers along one plane.

clue.text: Women he will meet not once or at any time

explanation.surface: A woman and a man may never meet, or might do so whenever they like.
explanation.definitionFit: The conjunction means on any occasion that, or at any time at all.

clue.text: A dry conclusion is frequent

explanation.surface: A dull ending happens often.
explanation.definitionFit: To frequent a place is to go there regularly, as one goes to a church or school.
